items.title: Bakhmut
items.text: After months of assaults led by the Wagner Group, Russian forces take most of Bakhmut. Some military analysts call it the bloodiest battle since World War II.

items.title: Kakhovka dam destroyed
items.text: The Russian-held Kakhovka dam is breached, flooding the lower Dnipro. Many experts concluded Russian forces likely blew it up; Russia denies this.
items.source: Wikipedia: Destruction of the Kakhovka Dam

items.title: Counteroffensive stalls
items.text: Ukraine's summer offensive in Zaporizhzhia and Donetsk meets dense minefields and trenches. It retakes 14 villages, about 370 km².

items.title: Avdiivka
items.text: Ukraine withdraws from Avdiivka, near Donetsk, after a four-month Russian offensive: Russia's largest gain since Bakhmut.

items.title: Towards Pokrovsk
items.text: Russian forces capture Prohres, north-west of Avdiivka, and push towards Pokrovsk, a road and rail hub of western Donetsk.

items.title: Ukraine enters Kursk
items.text: Ukraine launches an incursion into Russia's Kursk region. By March 2025 most Ukrainian forces had been pushed out. (Fighting in Russia is not on the control map.)

items.title: Pokrovsk and Myrnohrad
items.text: Russian forces enter Pokrovsk in November 2025 and are reported to have taken Pokrovsk and Myrnohrad in early 2026.

note: The long front, 2023 to 2026. Hand-entered by Orbis; each card names the article or record it was checked against (Wikipedia articles as retrieved on 2026-10-14, text paraphrased). Dates are Gregorian. Built by tools/build/ua_events.py.
